Going to the beach in the rain

A winter motorcycle ride to Ocean Shores

View all 10 photos

Photo 1 of 10: A few brave and hardy souls on the broad beach at Ocean Shores beneath an overcast sky.

Explore this trip and all others in ADV Atlas →

For a long time, some friends had been telling us about the best trip they did each year: choose a nice place in a terrible time of year and enjoy a relaxing few days just being, watching old movies, and hanging out. It was an interesting idea, to avoid any sense of missing something somewhere by going when there is nothing to miss.

In February 2024 they invited us along to Ocean Shores, a small tourist town on the Washington coast that makes Seattleites think of sunny summer days on sand. Winter on the coast is dim and dreary with short days and wind-blown drizzle. It’s quiet, many places are closed, and there isn’t much to do other than watch the waves crash in the rain. It sounded like a lovely time with an excuse to stay inside.

Looking Back
Before Leaving#↑

In the fall of 2023 I had gotten my motorcycle license and in December got a Honda CB500X on Craigslist. I had been going for short rides in the Cascade foothills, but was eager to spend more time on it, to actually take a trip on a motorcycle for the first time.

The forecast was wet and cold but I had a new, bright yellow Aerostich suit that made me look like a Power Ranger and the optimism that only comes with inexperience.

I had gone that way many times and knew I wanted to take ferries and backroads as much as possible, but had never taken that route by motorcycle. It felt like an adventure.

Seattle to Ocean Shores#↑

(136 mi / 218 km)

A quick ride across town got me to the Fauntleroy ferry terminal. I was running late and this was my first time riding onto a ferry so I was a bit flustered juggling gloves/card/ticket, but I made it on. One of the neat things about riding a motorcycle around the Puget Sound is that they always have extra space for bicycles and motorcycles, regardless of reservations or not.

Fauntleroy is in the city and Southworth is in the woods. Immediately there are quiet country roads leading out across the Kitsap Peninsula. I took backroads through the middle, at one point having to double back due to a downed Douglas Fir blocking the road.

As I cut inland west of Shelton, the temperatures dropped. I had to stop at a country gas station and warm up with a terrible, but hot, cup of coffee at one point and decided to turn down Highway 12 to just get to the coast. I arrived in town in a light rain that was deteriorating into a heavier one.

Getting off the motorcycle felt kind of like the end of a cold ski day: a deep chill that takes a hot shower to throw off. It wasn’t so many miles or even that long of a day, but it felt good to have woken up one place and ridden to another.

Photo gallery
My Honda CB500X leaves Fauntleroy on its first Washington ferry trip.
The mountain is out, but the weather looks iffy. Mount Rainier seen across the water.
Mount Baker visible beyond Puget Sound to the north from the ferry. It looks much nicer up there.
A Few Days in Ocean Shores#↑

We puttered around town for a few days, walked on the beach, and explored a little, but mostly cozied up inside, watched movies, and tended the fire.

Photo gallery
A few brave and hardy souls on the broad beach at Ocean Shores beneath an overcast sky.
Chainsaw bear figures beside the road during the ride through western Washington.
Yup. A roadside bear figure holding a carved wooden rifle.
A large asparagus for sale hand-painted sign, but I didn't see any actual asparagus for sale.
A wetland bog behind the dunes under gray winter skies near Ocean Shores.
A maze drawn in the wet sand on the beach near Ocean Shores.
The Ride Home: Ocean Shores back to Seattle#↑

(170 mi / 274 km)

I got a good start heading back in the morning and rode east back towards Seattle. In that area, the southern slopes of the Olympic Mountains, there are a number of rivers that have cut deep valleys leaving a sawtooth of ridges between. The road network does its best trying to connect them all, leaving beautiful and quiet roads hidden in a tunnel of Western Red Cedar.

The riding was very good following those ridges and valleys: the Hoquiam, the Wishkah, the Wynoochee, the Satsop, and their forks. The roads were quiet and mostly in good condition but the wet weather ensured a calm country cruise rather than anything more spirited.

Crossing onto the Peninsula again, it was cool and raining on and off, but the route along the Hood Canal was beautiful and moody. I was planning on taking the Bremerton ferry back to town, but just missed it and decided to ride around to Bainbridge rather than wait it out in the rain. The detour felt like a blow at the time, but ended up with a beautiful skyline in the dimming light as the ferry arrived at Colman Dock.

The Seattle skyline viewed across the water on the return trip.
Looking Back#↑

Overall it was a great trip. Our friends really are on to something. In the future we will have to copy their idea and take trips like that.

Despite the weather, it felt like an accomplishment to go somewhere distant on the motorcycle. I learned a bit about how to plan out routes, my own comfort, and the gear I should bring along (though mostly leave at home).

The forecast was wet and cold but I had a new, bright yellow Aerostich suit that made me look like a Power Ranger and the optimism that only comes with inexperience.

I had gone that way many times and knew I wanted to take ferries and backroads as much as possible, but had never taken that route by motorcycle. It felt like an adventure.

Seattle to Ocean Shores#↑

(136 mi / 218 km)

A quick ride across town got me to the Fauntleroy ferry terminal. I was running late and this was my first time riding onto a ferry so I was a bit flustered juggling gloves/card/ticket, but I made it on. One of the neat things about riding a motorcycle around the Puget Sound is that they always have extra space for bicycles and motorcycles, regardless of reservations or not.

Fauntleroy is in the city and Southworth is in the woods. Immediately there are quiet country roads leading out across the Kitsap Peninsula. I took backroads through the middle, at one point having to double back due to a downed Douglas Fir blocking the road.

As I cut inland west of Shelton, the temperatures dropped. I had to stop at a country gas station and warm up with a terrible, but hot, cup of coffee at one point and decided to turn down Highway 12 to just get to the coast. I arrived in town in a light rain that was deteriorating into a heavier one.

Getting off the motorcycle felt kind of like the end of a cold ski day: a deep chill that takes a hot shower to throw off. It wasn’t so many miles or even that long of a day, but it felt good to have woken up one place and ridden to another.

Photo gallery
My Honda CB500X leaves Fauntleroy on its first Washington ferry trip.
The mountain is out, but the weather looks iffy. Mount Rainier seen across the water.
Mount Baker visible beyond Puget Sound to the north from the ferry. It looks much nicer up there.
A Few Days in Ocean Shores#↑

We puttered around town for a few days, walked on the beach, and explored a little, but mostly cozied up inside, watched movies, and tended the fire.

Photo gallery
A few brave and hardy souls on the broad beach at Ocean Shores beneath an overcast sky.
Chainsaw bear figures beside the road during the ride through western Washington.
Yup. A roadside bear figure holding a carved wooden rifle.
A large asparagus for sale hand-painted sign, but I didn't see any actual asparagus for sale.
A wetland bog behind the dunes under gray winter skies near Ocean Shores.
A maze drawn in the wet sand on the beach near Ocean Shores.
The Ride Home: Ocean Shores back to Seattle#↑

(170 mi / 274 km)

I got a good start heading back in the morning and rode east back towards Seattle. In that area, the southern slopes of the Olympic Mountains, there are a number of rivers that have cut deep valleys leaving a sawtooth of ridges between. The road network does its best trying to connect them all, leaving beautiful and quiet roads hidden in a tunnel of Western Red Cedar.

The riding was very good following those ridges and valleys: the Hoquiam, the Wishkah, the Wynoochee, the Satsop, and their forks. The roads were quiet and mostly in good condition but the wet weather ensured a calm country cruise rather than anything more spirited.

Crossing onto the Peninsula again, it was cool and raining on and off, but the route along the Hood Canal was beautiful and moody. I was planning on taking the Bremerton ferry back to town, but just missed it and decided to ride around to Bainbridge rather than wait it out in the rain. The detour felt like a blow at the time, but ended up with a beautiful skyline in the dimming light as the ferry arrived at Colman Dock.

The Seattle skyline viewed across the water on the return trip.
Looking Back#↑

Overall it was a great trip. Our friends really are on to something. In the future we will have to copy their idea and take trips like that.

Despite the weather, it felt like an accomplishment to go somewhere distant on the motorcycle. I learned a bit about how to plan out routes, my own comfort, and the gear I should bring along (though mostly leave at home).
